To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of linguistic field work data for creating NLP tools can be very efficient, (2) that the quality of NLP tools created in this way can be very high, and that (3) the use of field work data can be a very efficient way to bootstrap the creation of NLP tools.

we were able to train a morphosyntactic parser and a dependency parser for Ingush using limited training data, and that we are able to improve the quality of our models with the help of additional data from linguistic field work.
we have created a morphological tagger, a dependency parser and a part-of-speech tagger for Ingush, using only a few hundred annotated sentences as training data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we create a dependency parser for a low-resource language? How can we leverage existing resources for NLP in other languages? How can we use linguistic fieldwork data to train NLP tools?

this paper presents a very interesting idea of using linguistic field work data to create NLP tools for low-resource languages, but that the work is still in its infancy and more research is necessary to make this a viable approach.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are currently able to produce a dependency treebank for Ingush from very little training data, which we use to train a dependency parser that is able to achieve 70.3% UAS and 64.1% LAS on the test data.
we are currently in the process of creating the first NLP tools for Ingush, and we have shown that it is possible to do so using very little annotated data.
we have developed an approach that allows to create NLP resources for low-resource languages from sparse linguistic field work data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the linguistic field work data we use as training resources is of high quality and can be used to train NLP tools with good performance.
the use of linguistic field work materials as a resource for NLP can be very beneficial for under-resourced low-resource languages.
it is possible to create NLP tools with very little annotated training data, and that it is possible with the help of linguistic field work to create such data.
